chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Ishaq al-Alawi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Suleiman al-Daylami, from Fureyt, from Ibn Abi Yafour, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when a man from the otter hunters came to him and said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you, what do you say regarding the Salat in the otter (fur)?' So he said, 'There is no problem with the Salat in it.' The man said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you, it is dead, and it is my profession, and I understand it.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'I know it better than you.' The man said, 'It is my profession, and there is none who knows it better than I.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) smiled, then said to him, 'Do you say that it is an animal that comes out of the water, or is caught from the water, and when the water is lost [or it is removed from water], it dies?' The man said, 'You speak the truth, may I be sacrificed for you, this is how it is.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'So you say that it is an animal that walks on four, and it is not like the fish, so its slaughter is its exit from the water?' The man said, 'Yes, by Allah, this is what I say.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Indeed, Allah, Blessed and High, has permitted it and made its slaughter its death, just as He has permitted the fish and made their slaughter their death.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray in clothing made from the fur of an otter?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) resolves a juristic nuance regarding the purity of otter fur by distinguishing between aquatic animals and semi-aquatic mammals. He establishes that since the otter is a four-legged beast whose life is bound to water, its ritual slaughter is equated with its death, mirroring the ruling for fish. This highlights the Shia scholarly principle of adapting legal classifications based on biological characteristics rather than rigid categorical boundaries.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Abdullah Bin Is’haq Al Alawy, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Muhammad Bin Suleyman Al Daylami, from Fureyt, from Ibn Abu Yafour who said,

‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullahasws when a man from the otter hunters came over to himasws, and he said to himasws, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! What are youasws saying regarding the Salāt in the otter (fur)?’ So heasws said, ‘There is no problem with the Salāt in it. So the man said to himasws, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! It is dead, and it is my profession, and I understand it’. So Abu Abdullahasws said to him: ‘Iasws more understanding with it than you do’. So the man said to him, ‘It is my profession, and there is none more understanding with it than I am’. So Abu Abdullahasws smiled, then said to him: ‘You are saying that it is an animal coming out from the water, or being hunted from the water, so when it comes out and misses the water, it dies’. So he said, ‘Youasws speak the truth, may I be scarified for youasws! This is how it is’. So Abu Abdullahasws said to him: ‘So you are saying that it is an animal walking upon four, and it is not upon a limit of the fish, so its purification is its exit from the water?’ So the man said, ‘Yes, by Allahazwj! It is like this’. So Abu Abdullahasws said to him: ‘But Allahazwj Blessed and High has Permitted it, and Made its purification to be (upon) its death, just as Heazwj has Permitted the fish and Made its purification, (upon) its death’.
en.sarwar: 11. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Ishaq al-‘Alaviy from al-Hassan ibn Ali from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al- Daylamiy from Furayt from ibn abu Ya‘fur who has said the following:

“Once I was in the presence of abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when a man of al-Khazzazin came and said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, ‘What do you say about performing Salah (prayer) with al-Khazz? He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not an offense to perform Salah (prayer) with it.’ A man then said to him (the Imam), ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, it is dead and it is manufactured and I know it. Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘I know it more than you do.’ The man said, ‘It is manufactured and no one knows more than I know.’ Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, then smiled and asked, ‘Do you say that it is an animal that comes from water? Or you say that it is caught from water and is brought out and when it is away from water it dies?’ The man said, ‘You spoke the truth, I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, that is how it is.’ Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said to him, ‘So you say that it is an animal that walks on four feet and it is not like whales in the case of which its properly being slaughtered is its coming out of the water.’ The man said, ‘Yes, by Allah that is what I say how it is.’ Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘Allah, most High has made it lawful and its proper slaughtering is its dying like whales for which proper slaughtering is its dying.’”
